A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EchoingPixels work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen2.5-Omni benchmark evaluations, latency and memory measurements, component ablations, and appendix experiments on frequency partitioning and encoder depth.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, encoder and selection ablations, positional-encoding comparisons, and measurements across video durations.

M1.justification: Both versions use copied bidirectional LLM layers, an MLP scorer, joint-pool Top-K selection trained with STE, preserved text tokens, and the same [18,18,18,10] Sync-RoPE partition. v2's extractive-selection terminology, positional-index clarification, and spectral interpretation do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Training retains the same LLaVA-Video/Ola, AVQA, and FortisAVQA mixture. Evaluation retains WorldSense, Daily-Omni, Video-MME with and without audio, and MLVU-dev. The added controls and duration sweep analyze the existing audio-visual/video tasks without introducing another dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated PyramidDrop and OmniZip baselines, FastV-tuned, and the TMRoPE-I positional-encoding comparator. FastV itself already appeared in v1's appendix. The extended standalone-model comparisons against Unified-IO-2, VideoLLaMA2, Vita-1.5, and Ola are dropped, although selected reference scores remain in prose.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands controlled evaluation through matched-data FastV fine-tuning, additional attention/selection/frequency configurations, a 3B/20%-budget latency sweep over 5–60 seconds, and the wrapped-distance diagnostic in Appendix B.4. Existing benchmark protocols and main training settings remain unchanged; the effective-frame-rate explanation is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: New analyses test causal attention and removal of text pre-fusion, random/similarity/Gumbel-Softmax selection, interleaved positional frequencies, training fairness, and duration-dependent latency. Figure 4 adds a positional-aliasing diagnostic. The frequency-partition and encoder-depth studies already existed in v1's appendix, and the qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 4 and Appendix B.4 newly report the mean and standard deviation of a wrapped-distance proxy across temporal channels. These bands describe channel dispersion, not uncertainty across experimental runs. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerous comparator and diagnostic results, including FastV-tuned's 91.9% relative performance and TMRoPE-I's 57.89 Daily-Omni score. Existing EchoingPixels headline accuracy and average latency results remain unchanged. Encoder depth N=2 changes from 93.0% to 92.8% relative performance; v1's explicit OCR-score comparison and extended standalone-model result rows are removed.

T1.justification: v1 provides the RoPE identity and a qualitative oscillation argument. v2 adds local-stride definitions, phase-collision reasoning, a Nyquist inequality, frequency/wavelength calculations in Appendix A, and the wrapped-distance definition in Appendix B.4. Section 3.2 also introduces claimed global monotonicity and bijectivity guarantees for the retained design.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion reposition the contribution from adaptive joint-stream compression toward the claimed first systematic identification of positional aliasing and a mathematically derived correction. The retained 5–20% token-performance claim now supports a broader claim about theoretically grounded sparse learning.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning Nyquist violations, the importance of pre-fusion and learned selection, and training fairness. Appendix C.2 attributes TMRoPE-I's weakness to departure from pretrained positional patterns. A new Limitations section explicitly restricts direct application of Sync-RoPE to RoPE-based architectures.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, retained-token ordering and position-ID details, patch/frame-merging explanations, the Daily-Omni timing dataset and batch size, and new baseline implementation parameters. The effective 1 FPS explanation clarifies processing after the retained 2 FPS input sampling; it does not establish a changed sampling procedure.

R1.justification: Related work is recast around extractive versus abstractive compression and gains a multimodal positional-encoding subsection. New connections include Q-Former/BLIP-2, Shannon, VideoRoPE, HoPE, and OmniZip. v1's assertion that dedicated audio-visual compression work is absent gives way to a concurrent-work comparison and novelty claims about sparsification's spectral effects.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method rationale, results discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Ablations are reorganized across the main text and appendices, and new Limitations and Impact Statement sections alter the document structure.

P2.justification: v2 changes the paper template and appendix column layout, expands and restructures tables, adds the positional-aliasing plot, and substantially redesigns Figure 6. v1's compression-paradigm diagram is removed; its temporal-frequency plot and bidirectional examples are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through additional baselines, a matched-training FastV control, and targeted ablations, while improving implementation disclosure. However, v1's qualitative temporal explanation becomes a central mathematical guarantee in v2: Section 3.2 uses a representative or mean stride to claim global monotonicity for irregular gaps, without establishing the necessary maximum-gap or total-span bounds. The empirical gains and unsupported theoretical strengthening leave the net quality change uncertain.
